turns.t: Ah, hello doctor. It's this cough of mine, it's been going on forever. Six weeks, near enough.
Six weeks is a long time, you were right to come. Is it a dry cough or are you bringing anything up?
Dry, dry as a bone. Nothing comes up at all.
Is it worse at any time of day?
At night, mostly. It tickles in my throat when I lie down.
Have you had any fever, or been coughing up blood?
No fever, no blood, thank God.
And what tablets are you on at the moment?
Ramipril, 5 mg, once a day, for the blood pressure.
Thank you. You mentioned blood pressure, is that the only long-term problem?
That's the one. Blood pressure, for about eight years.
Are you a smoker?
I was, and I still have the odd one if I'm out with the girls.
Roughly how many would you have in a week?
Och, not many. Five, maybe six.
I see. And has the cough been interfering with your sleep? ~
It has, yes. My husband has moved into the spare room. ~
That sounds miserable for both of you. Let me listen to your chest for a moment. ~
Go on.
I'll arrange a chest X-ray, just to be sure there's nothing in the lungs that I can't hear.
Will that take long? ~
It's very quick. You can have it done at the hospital this week, no appointment needed. ~
That's grand. And what about the cough itself? ~
There is a possibility that the ramipril is causing it, because dry coughs are a known side effect, but we should check the X-ray first.
I never knew that. ~
Many people don't. Please don't stop it by yourself, we'll talk after the X-ray.
I won't, I promise. ~
Would you like to talk about cutting down on the smoking at the same time? ~
Not today, doctor, if you don't mind. ~
That's fine. The offer is there whenever you want it. ~
Thank you. You're very kind. ~
If you start coughing up blood, or get breathless, come back straight away.
I will, I will. ~
